newsitem.title: GERMANY: NCA raised ex-Germany cargo rates 7pct.
newsitem.headline: NCA raised ex-Germany cargo rates 7pct.

text.p: Nippon Cargo Airlines said it has increased rates to Japan by seven percent effective March 1.
Meinholf Weiden, sales manager Germany, said the rise was prompted by soaring market demand, tight space and internal demands for a better yield.
NCA had been swamped with cargo requests for February and March in recent weeks, he added.
"VAT in Japan will rise to five percent from three percent from April so many companies are trying to increase imports in March to avoid this," he told Reuters.
"Agents are booking one tonne and then coming to us with two and a half," he added.
But the fall in the German mark against the yen compared to the stable rates of other European currencies meant German cargo was financially less attractive for the airline.
"Rates in Germany are going up but yields from other countries are better," Weiden said.
"Whoever pays more gains more space. So we have to fight not only against competitors but with other (NCA) stations," he said. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
